abstention.statement: There is no evidence connecting ABCB9 or OR8J3 to dilated cardiomyopathy. ABCB9 is an ATP-dependent peptide transporter primarily found in lysosomes, and single-cell profiling of the heart reveals negligible detection in cardiac cell types from dilated cardiomyopathy patients. OR8J3 is an odorant receptor with no detectable transcript in heart tissue. Furthermore, neither gene possesses genetic association scores in Open Targets for this disease, nor any hits in the GWAS Catalog, and their perturbation in model organisms yields no relevant cardiac phenotypes.
abstention.what_would_change_this: Evidence of ABCB9 or OR8J3 variants co-segregating with dilated cardiomyopathy in a familial cohort, supported by altered cardiac function upon targeted deletion in a mammalian model organism.

chain.note: RBM20 regulates alternative splicing of TTN mRNA in cardiomyocytes.

falsification.description: Deplete RBM20 in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes using CRISPR interference and evaluate if the resulting TTN mis-splicing leads to reduced contractile force; attempt rescue by introducing a properly spliced TTN cDNA.

hypotheses.mechanism: RBM20 is an RNA-binding protein that regulates the alternative splicing of TTN in cardiomyocytes. Loss of RBM20 function leads to mis-splicing of TTN, which compromises the structural integrity and extensibility of the cardiac sarcomere, ultimately leading to the development of dilated cardiomyopathy.
hypotheses.title: RBM20 regulates TTN splicing to maintain sarcomere integrity

chain.note: TNNT2 confers calcium-sensitivity to the actomyosin ATPase complex, of which MYH7 is the primary motor.

falsification.description: Introduce a loss-of-function mutation in TNNT2 in a 3D engineered heart tissue model and measure changes in calcium sensitivity and MYH7 ATPase activity, determining whether restoring calcium sensitivity prevents the loss of contractile force.

hypotheses.mechanism: TNNT2 is a troponin subunit that confers calcium sensitivity to the actomyosin ATPase complex, of which MYH7 is the primary cardiac motor protein. Disruption of the interaction between TNNT2 and MYH7 impairs the calcium-dependent regulation of muscle contraction, leading to decreased cardiac contractility and dilated cardiomyopathy.
hypotheses.title: TNNT2 regulates MYH7 actomyosin ATPase activity for cardiac contractility

chain.note: Lamins provide a structural framework for the nuclear envelope.

falsification.description: Subject human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes with LMNA truncation mutations to cyclic mechanical stretch and measure the rate of nuclear rupture and apoptosis compared to isogenic wild-type cells.

hypotheses.mechanism: LMNA forms the structural meshwork of the nuclear lamina, conferring mechanical stiffness to the nucleus in cardiomyocytes. Mutations in LMNA disrupt this framework, rendering the nuclear envelope vulnerable to the mechanical stress of muscle contraction, which disrupts cardiac homeostasis and leads to dilated cardiomyopathy.
hypotheses.title: LMNA maintains nuclear envelope integrity required for cardiac homeostasis
